mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the next month reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the 20-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by 0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 30-day period of lower rates (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rates (UNRATE) reduce consumer and business confidence, lowering expected future earnings and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive despite UNRATE above 5.5% for 30 consecutive days (Rank IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests weakening domestic demand, which precedes a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return when combined with a concurrent drop in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL).
failure_condition: Interaction effect rank correlation < 0.2 over 1000 windows of 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) indicates supply-side constraints that raise production costs and reduce corporate profit expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 3-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 3%, it signals a shift to accommodative policy, associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the policy signal (Rank IC < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in job openings (PAYEMS) above 7 million coincides with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as strong labor market conditions support corporate optimism.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during the prior 30-day period of lower openings (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) erode purchasing power, generating negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns unless offset by a stronger than expected earnings beat (GDPC1).
failure_condition: Interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in 500 sliding 20-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle regime (as indicated by FEDFUNDS trajectory), S&P 500 20-day forward returns tend to be negative regardless of other macro signals.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS is in an upward trend over the last 6 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 40% of tightening periods (quantile split).
